tickets.title: [Workstream F] Wire adlc model-router into tier assignment (lib/plan.mjs / lib/pools.mjs)
tickets.body:
handoff.md (this repo, root) is the authoritative design for this ticket. Read it in full before starting — do not re-derive the target integration model, gap analysis, or sequencing. Treat its numbered tasks and acceptance criteria as the contract; this ticket body summarizes and adds verification commands, it does not replace it. Implements handoff.md §5 Workstream F, task 1 (highest payoff-order item).

Booster's tier heuristics (which pool/model a ticket routes to) are currently bespoke, hand-rolled in lib/pools.mjs. Replace or cross-check against adlc model-router's frontier/direct/ladder strategy assignment.

ACCEPTANCE CRITERIA:
- AC1: lib/plan.mjs's tier-assignment step calls adlc model-router (or cross-checks its output) instead of relying solely on lib/pools.mjs heuristics. VERIFY: a test stubs the CLI, asserts it's invoked with the ticket set, and asserts the resulting tier assignment reflects its output.
- AC2: Before/after behavior documented in docs/guidelines.md. VERIFY: grep for a "model-router" section.
- AC3: npm test exits 0, no regression to existing plan.mjs tests.

tickets.title: [Workstream F] Replace two-strike regeneration trigger with adlc flail-detector
tickets.body:
handoff.md (this repo, root) is the authoritative design for this ticket. Read it in full before starting — do not re-derive the target integration model, gap analysis, or sequencing. Treat its numbered tasks and acceptance criteria as the contract; this ticket body summarizes and adds verification commands, it does not replace it. Implements handoff.md §5 Workstream F, task 3.

Booster's bespoke "two-strike regeneration" trigger (a failed-gate counter) in lib/scheduler.mjs should be replaced with adlc flail-detector's principled detection of repeated errors, scope violations, edit churn, and oversized logs.

COORDINATION NOTE: this ticket touches lib/scheduler.mjs, the same file T-B modifies. Land after T-B merges to avoid a large merge conflict; this is a sequencing note, not a DAG edge, since flail-detector and rail-enforcement wiring touch different functions in the same file.

ACCEPTANCE CRITERIA:
- AC1: The two-strike counter is replaced (or backed) by adlc flail-detector's signal on the builder's log. VERIFY: a test feeds a fixture log with repeated errors/scope violations to flail-detector and asserts the scheduler's regeneration trigger fires on its verdict, not just a raw failure count.
- AC2: A false-trigger fixture (single transient failure, no flail pattern) does NOT trigger regeneration. VERIFY: test asserts no regeneration for a one-off failure.
- AC3: npm test exits 0.

tickets.title: [Workstream F] Fan out candidate fixes via adlc consensus-fix instead of single-attempt regeneration
tickets.body:
handoff.md (this repo, root) is the authoritative design for this ticket. Read it in full before starting — do not re-derive the target integration model, gap analysis, or sequencing. Treat its numbered tasks and acceptance criteria as the contract; this ticket body summarizes and adds verification commands, it does not replace it. Implements handoff.md §5 Workstream F, task 4.

The one-shot fix-round after a failed prosecution (lib/scheduler.mjs's current single-attempt fix loop) should fan out multiple candidate fixes via adlc consensus-fix and pick the gated consensus winner instead of trusting one regeneration.

ACCEPTANCE CRITERIA:
- AC1: On a failed prosecution, the scheduler invokes adlc consensus-fix (fan-out candidates) rather than a single regeneration attempt. VERIFY: a test stubs the CLI, asserts invocation with the failing test command and changed files, and asserts the winning candidate is applied.
- AC2: If consensus-fix itself fails to converge (no winner), the scheduler falls back to the existing single-attempt path with a logged reason, not a silent hang. VERIFY: test simulates a no-consensus result, asserts fallback behavior and log entry.
- AC3: npm test exits 0.

tickets.title: [Workstream F] Record every gate as append-only evidence via adlc gate-manifest
tickets.body:
handoff.md (this repo, root) is the authoritative design for this ticket. Read it in full before starting — do not re-derive the target integration model, gap analysis, or sequencing. Treat its numbered tasks and acceptance criteria as the contract; this ticket body summarizes and adds verification commands, it does not replace it. Implements handoff.md §5 Workstream F, task 5.

Every gate a run already produces (pre-merge build, prosecution verdict, post-merge build, rollback) should be recorded as append-only, attestable evidence via adlc gate-manifest, not just .booster/report.json log lines. This is the audit trail T-E's CI gate and T-D's prosecution both want to point at.

ACCEPTANCE CRITERIA:
- AC1: Each gate outcome in a scheduler run is recorded via adlc gate-manifest record. VERIFY: a test stubs the CLI, asserts a record call per gate transition (build pass/fail, prosecution verdict, rollback) with the correct gate name and evidence payload.
- AC2: adlc gate-manifest show / verify can reconstruct a run's gate history from the manifest alone. VERIFY: run a fixture scheduler pass, then adlc gate-manifest show, assert it lists the expected gate sequence.
- AC3: npm test exits 0.

ACCEPTANCE CRITERIA:

- AC2: Documented in docs/guidelines.md as an opt-in periodic check, not part of every agb review invocation (cost). VERIFY: grep for a "review-calibration" section noting opt-in behavior.
